# Audit and proof: a zero-volume endpoint facet supplies a volume charge

The proposed facet-extrusion inequality is valid in the stated scope
d>=2 and proper captured A cut. It uses the actual supporting face,
not an independently assigned zero row. This note gives the proof and
records the lower-dimensional restriction explicitly.

Let A,K,B be full d-dimensional convex bodies with (A+B)/2 subset K.
Let u!=0, and take a through-source ambient cap whose A threshold is
t_A, whose B threshold is t_B, and whose K threshold is
t_K=(t_A+t_B)/2. Assume the A cut is proper and the B cap has zero
d-volume with supporting face

    F=B intersect {u.x=t_B},

of positive (d-1)-volume sigma_F. Write

    A^+=A intersect {u.x>=t_A}, U=|A^+|,
    h=max_(x in A) u.x,
    q=|K intersect {u.x>=t_K}|.

Then

    q >= 2^(-d) [ U+sigma_F*(h-t_A)/||u|| ].        (1)

In the plane the bracket is exactly |A^++F|. In higher dimensions
there are additional nonnegative mixed terms in the slice estimate.

Proof. Every midpoint of A^+ and F belongs to K and has u-coordinate
at least t_K. Hence (A^++F)/2 lies inside the captured K cap. Choose
orthogonal coordinates with last coordinate s=u.x/||u||. Since F
lies at one fixed s-coordinate, every slice of A^++F is exactly the
corresponding slice of A^+ plus the fixed translated facet F, all in
one common (d-1)-space. If its slice area is v(s), ordinary BM gives

    |(A^+)_s+F|_(d-1)
       >= [v(s)^(1/(d-1))+sigma_F^(1/(d-1))]^(d-1)
       >= v(s)+sigma_F.

The slices are full (d-1)-dimensional for the interior of the normal
range; its endpoints have one-dimensional parameter measure zero.
Properness of the original cap makes this range have exactly length
(h-t_A)/||u||. Fubini and integration of the displayed inequality
therefore give |A^++F|>=U+sigma_F(h-t_A)/||u||. Homothety by 1/2
scales d-volume by 2^(-d), which proves (1). For d=2 the slice sets
are intervals, whose lengths add exactly, giving the claimed equality
before the final containment in K.

In the normalized planar all-zero-endpoint simplex configuration,
t_A=-1, t_B=1, t_K=0. For B=T={x<=1,y<=1,-x-y<=1}, its three
facet lengths are 3||v_i||. If U_i is the corresponding A cap area
and h_i=max_A v_i.x, (1) becomes

    q_i >= [U_i+3(h_i+1)]/4.                       (2)

For a common actual mixed cap mass Q=U_i+q_i, this is exactly

    4Q >= 5U_i+3(h_i+1).                          (3)

If B occupies only a proper segment of the containing T facet, its
actual length replaces 3||v_i||; filling the whole containing facet
without proof is not permitted.

The case d=1 is excluded: a supporting face then has dimension zero,
and addition of a single point does not contribute another interval
length. The formula with both U and an added width would be false.
For a strictly full A capture, one must use its true lower support
value instead of t_A unless equality with that threshold is verified.
Empty A captures and lower-dimensional nonproper A sections are not
used to infer a positive width charge. These status restrictions are
essential and are satisfied in the proposed proper-cut application.

No smoothness, rationality, positive lattice width, or general-position
assumption is used. Normalization by ||u|| is necessary for oblique
continuous normals and has been tracked explicitly.
